## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Olmo 3](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13961>)

Olmo 3 releases an end-to-end model development pipeline with separate pretraining, targeted mid-training, context extension, and post-training stages, together with data and intermediate checkpoints. Its short continuation experiments and integration tests provide a reproducible way to choose data mixtures and measure capability tradeoffs before committing to a full training run.

**Published:** 2025-12-15 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Mid-training, Data Mixtures, Open Training, Long Context

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13961>) · [Blog](<https://allenai.org/blog/olmo3>) · [Code](<https://github.com/allenai/OLMo-core>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. The April 14, 2026 paper revision documents stage-level comparisons, data filtering, continuation ablations, and domain tradeoffs; public code and checkpoints make it a useful open training reference.

**Limitations:** Recipe development focuses on 7B and 32B models, with substantial compute requirements; improvements on one data domain can reduce performance on others, and release-time leadership claims are not treated as current rankings.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension](<https://allenai.org/papers/olmpool>)

OlmPool holds data and context-extension procedures fixed across 26 comparable models to test how normalization, grouped-query attention, sliding windows, and pretraining context length affect later long-context ability. The results show why a context-extension recipe should be validated on the intended architecture early, since ordinary short-context metrics can miss substantial downstream weaknesses.

**Published:** 2026-04-23 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Long Context, Architecture, Controlled Ablations

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://allenai.org/papers/olmpool>) · [Blog](<https://allenai.org/blog/olmpool>) · [Code](<https://github.com/allenai/olmpool>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The full report provides paired architectural comparisons and HELMET, RULER, and long-context perplexity results, with model configurations and before/after checkpoints released. Its publication date is corroborated by the linked Ai2 author announcement dated April 23, 2026; the inspected report front matter is undated.

**Limitations:** The controlled suite centers on approximately 7B dense models and one data/extension setup; these findings do not establish that the same architectural choices are universally harmful at other scales or training budgets.
